guidelineReference: SJA First Aid / minor allergic reaction
title: Mild pollen allergy at a temple fun day
setting: Sikh temple children's fun day. A pre-teen child walks up to you with streaming, watery eyes, sneezing repeatedly. Patient is alert and responsive.
verdictExplanation: Alert, responsive, stable observations. Mild localized allergic reaction to pollen (hayfever) with no airway, breathing, or circulation red flags. Treat on scene.

shared.circulation: Skin around eyes is red, watery eyes

er.exposure: Outdoors, hot summer day next to flower stands

history.history: Triggered by flower stand pollen on a hot summer day at the fun day
history.drugs: Takes daily antihistamine (forgot to take his dose today)
history.additional: Parent is nearby at the bouncy castle

followUp.question: What is the appropriate first aid management for this mild pollen allergy?

options.text: Move him away from the flower stands into a cool indoor area, wash his face with cold water, and locate his parent
Call 999 for a priority emergency response
Lie him flat on his back, elevate his legs, and prepare the AED
Force him to use a stranger's adrenaline auto-injector as a precaution

followUp.explanation: Mild localized allergies are managed by removing the trigger (move indoors/away from flowers), washing eyes/face with cold water to soothe, and coordinating with parents for their regular antihistamine. 999 and AED are completely inappropriate for hayfever. Adrenaline is only for life-threatening anaphylaxis.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Wash face and eyes. Locate parents so they can administer his antihistamine. Reassure.
levelFlags.erNotes: Ensure BGL is normal. Check for signs of worsening (wheeze, lip swelling). Discharge with advice once parents are present.
